clue.text: Papa in novel tries wit

indicators.note: novel means new or unfamiliar, so the following word is to be made into something new by rearranging
in tells us one piece sits inside the other rather than beside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Papa is the NATO alphabet word for P

explanation.surface: A writer of fiction has another go at being funny, with Papa featuring in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPRIT is a French borrowing used in English for lively cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit means quick, lively intelligence and sparkle in conversation, a close synonym for humour and cleverness.

clue.text: Odd number observed, divided by five

indicators.note: a word divided by something is split apart with that thing placed in the gap

blocks.note: observed means seen
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone notices an odd number and sees it split by five, like a maths puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven cannot be divided evenly by two, so it is one example of an uneven integer.

clue.text: Super-evil Machiavellian, nasty

indicators.note: Machiavellian means scheming and devious, suggesting the preceding letters have been cunningly twisted around

blocks.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the hyphen, are the raw material

explanation.surface: A cartoon supervillain is described as scheming and unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive describes something disgusting or deeply unpleasant, an adjective synonym of the clue word.

clue.text: Crude — like metal fasteners?

blocks.note: first meaning: cheap, tasteless and vulgar
second, playful meaning: resembling tacks, the small sharp nails, by adding -y to the noun

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is invented for fun: tacks plus the adjective ending -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky is everyday slang for cheap and vulgar, while the joke reading treats it as an adjective formed from tacks.

clue.text: Famous songwriter somewhere in Germany

blocks.note: first meaning: Irving ..., writer of White Christmas
second meaning: the German capital city

explanation.surface: A celebrated composer is spotted at an unnamed spot in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was a celebrated American composer of popular music, and the same name is the capital of the German state.

clue.text: Revelation, beautiful woman

blocks.note: first meaning: a shocking piece of news
second meaning: an informal word for a very attractive woman

explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is both a startling surprise disclosure and slang for a strikingly glamorous female.

clue.text: Note held by king changed recording

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message handed to a monarch has been altered, or a royal tape doctored.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a new version of a track made by altering and rebalancing the original audio.

clue.text: Leg in a net, tangled up — graceless

indicators.note: things tangled up are twisted out of their tidy order

blocks.note: the letters of these four words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone has caught a limb in a net and is flailing clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking poise or style, a direct adjective synonym for clumsy and unrefined.

clue.text: Porter regularly going over lovely, small building

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so we keep every other letter of the word

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Porter
fab is short for fabulous, meaning lovely

explanation.surface: A hotel porter strolls past a pleasant little building.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue going over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house assembled from factory parts, typically a modest single-storey structure.

clue.text: Malodorous coloured liquid filling malodorous place

indicators.note: something filling another is stuffed inside it

blocks.note: a pigsty is a notoriously smelly spot
ink is a liquid coloured for writing

explanation.surface: Something smelly and dyed is being poured into an already smelly place.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated adjective is a trap: the first is the definition, the second belongs to a wordplay phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinky is an informal word for having a strong, unpleasant odour, matching the formal adjective.

clue.text: Encourage minister in the lead

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a title for a minister of religion
a team that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A clergyman is urged on while out in front, perhaps in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To rev someone up is to stir them into enthusiasm and energy, the phrasal-verb sense of urging on.

clue.text: French food associate fed to pet

indicators.note: something fed to an animal goes inside it

blocks.note: a cat is a typical household pet
a member is an associate of a club or society

explanation.surface: Someone feeds a colleague's French snack to the family animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft creamy cheese from Normandy, so it is a specific example of French fare.

clue.text: North America circumnavigated by horse in the end

indicators.note: a thing circumnavigated is travelled all the way round, so it ends up enclosed

blocks.note: a filly is a young female horse
NA is the standard abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: A continent is ridden round on horseback, a journey completed at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally and the idiom both mean eventually, after a long time or at the conclusion.

clue.text: Number nine, peg between two poles

indicators.note: between puts the middle pieces inside the two that flank them

blocks.note: S for south, the first of the two poles
IX is nine in Roman numerals
a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
N for north, the second of the two poles

explanation.surface: A numbered tent peg is staked out between two tent poles.
explanation.walkthrough: The two poles are South and North, one placed on each side of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixteen is a cardinal figure, so it is one example of the general word for a quantity.

clue.text: Moved to balmier US city

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted into different positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone relocated in search of a warmer climate in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved to' reads as a single verb phrase, but 'to' is part of the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a port city in the state of Maryland in the eastern United States.

clue.text: House, as central, demolished

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked apart and its pieces left jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A centrally located home has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: House here means a royal dynasty, not a building, which is what 'demolished' pushes you towards.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English royal dynasty, one side in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Endless fruit and a nut in a stew for primate

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
to be in a stew is to be in a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: an orange is a citrus fruit
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fruit and nuts are thrown into a stew meant to feed an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan is a red-haired great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, so it is one kind of primate.

clue.text: Country where some fifty Latinos retired

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted, a run of consecutive letters
retired means drawn back, so the letters are taken backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A nation where fifty Latin Americans have gone to spend their retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a nation in southern Europe, so it is an example of the general word for a state.

clue.text: One’s gin and it designed for drinking, perhaps

indicators.note: something designed is planned out and arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth is mixed specially for someone to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a classic British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth; the 'and' is left out of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingestion is taking something into the body by mouth, of which swallowing a drink is one instance.

clue.text: Delicate material around balloon ultimately burst

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps about the other
ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
the final letter of balloon

explanation.surface: Fine fabric wrapped round a balloon finally makes it pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst' looks like describing the balloon, but it is the definition: lancing a boil bursts it open.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce a boil or abscess with a blade so that it opens and drains.

clue.text: Painful struggles of one expecting work

blocks.note: first meaning: childbirth, the efforts of a woman expecting a baby
second meaning: toil or hard physical effort

explanation.walkthrough: 'One expecting' means a pregnant woman, not someone waiting for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is the process of giving birth and also a general noun for hard toil or employment.

clue.text: Wild gorilla snatching at reptile

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the following letters run riot
snatching means grabbing and holding something inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild ape lunges and grabs at a crocodile-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian of the Americas and China, an example of a cold-blooded scaly animal.

clue.text: Appearing more flushed, running up and down just the same?

definitions.text: running up and down just the same?

blocks.note: first meaning: having a ruddier face

blocks.clueFragment: running up and down just the same?
blocks.note: second, cryptic meaning: a down entry that reads identically whether you go up or down, a palindrome

explanation.surface: Someone running up and down a hill gets more and more red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests exercise, but it describes the letters running in the grid: this word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Redder is the comparative of red, describing a face that has grown pinker with exertion or embarrassment.

clue.text: Slowing down, top dog in the underwear industry?

blocks.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
surface padding that turns the charade into a picture of a business tycoon
the top dog is the one in charge

explanation.surface: A business leader in lingerie is pictured easing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a whimsical charade: the boss of the underwear trade would be a bra king.
explanation.definitionFit: Braking is applying the brakes to reduce a vehicle's speed, a present participle matching the clue phrase.

clue.text: Sweet thing in cakes is needed, getting topping on those?

definitions.text: Sweet thing in cakes is needed, getting topping on those?

indicators.note: the topping of each word is its first letter, so we take only the heads of those words

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A baker reflects that cakes need a sugary coating on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: read straight, it describes the sweet layer on a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread over cakes, the sweet layer applied as a topping.

clue.text: Celebrity confined to earth, hot stuff

indicators.note: something confined to a place is shut up inside it

blocks.note: mud is wet earth
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person, grounded at home, is still considered very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests a sexy celebrity, but it means a spicy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent yellow condiment, hot in the spicy sense of burning the tongue.

clue.text: Encoding device way above top of mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
the first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A secret coding machine is carried up a path above a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue above means placed before, so the first piece sits over the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem modulates digital data into signals for a phone line and back, so it converts information.

clue.text: A bit isolated

blocks.note: taken as written
a part is a bit or portion

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'somewhat isolated', but 'A bit' is the wordplay and the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated or set aside from others, an adjective sense close to cut off.

clue.text: To a certain extent, viscount ain’t educated — simple!

indicators.note: to a certain extent means only partly, so only a run of letters inside the next words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters running across these three words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dim aristocrat is mocked as having had no schooling at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' seems to describe the uneducated viscount, but it is the definition, in the sense of pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple can mean pure and unadulterated, and untainted means free from contamination or corruption.

clue.text: Furious speed passing third on grid

indicators.note: third tells us to keep only the letter in position three of the word

blocks.note: the third letter of grid
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: An angry racing driver speeds past the car in third on the starting grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' here means coming after, so the speed word follows the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, an adjective synonym for enraged and livid.

clue.text: Monster put on wrapping paper

indicators.note: wrapping means going round something and enclosing it

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone sets a monster mask down on gift-wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapping paper' looks like a single noun, but 'wrapping' is the signal and 'paper' a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fire-breathing winged beast of legend, one of the classic mythical creatures.

clue.text: Amount of time, very little

blocks.note: first meaning: sixty seconds
second meaning, pronounced differently: tiny

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt the same but said differently, one stressed on the first syllable and one on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is a sixty-second span of the clock, and minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means extremely small.
